newsitem.title: USA: Palo Verde nuke leaks water while shut, no hazard.
newsitem.headline: Palo Verde nuke leaks water while shut, no hazard.

text.p: Operators of the Palo Verde nuclear plant west of Phoenix, Ariz., said water leaked from one part of the plant's idled 1,270 megawatt (MW) unit 3 early Thursday, leading to notification of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
The "unusual event" declaration is the least serious of four emergency classifications under NRC guidelines.
The unit is currently shut down for scheduled refueling.

Palo Verde operator Arizona Public Service Co, which is owned by Pinnacle West Capital Corp, said about 10,000 gallons of water leaked past a seal on a gate that separates the spent fuel pool from an adjacent channel.
The company stressed that the leak posed no safety hazard, although nonessential workers were removed from the fuel building as a precaution.
"Our investigation is focused on why the seal leaked and making sure it doesn't happen again," said Jim Levine, the company's senior vice president of nuclear operations.

The Palo Verde plant, which has two other 1,270 MW units, is jointly owned by Arizona Public Service, Salt River Project, Southern California Edison Co, El Paso Electric Co, Public Service Co of New Mexico, Southern California Public Power Authority and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power.
